sections.heading: GeM Vendor Assessment Explained: Why RITES (Not QCI) Decides If You Sell on GeM in 2026
paragraphs: So you've done your GeM Registration. Your seller account is live. You're ready to list products and start winning government orders.
Then you try to list under a certain category, and GeM asks for something called "Vendor Assessment". No warning, no real explanation. Just a locked door where you expected a clear path.
Here's the good news: it's not as complicated as it looks. It's just a step nobody explains properly. Let's fix that.

GeM Vendor Assessment (VA) is a background check for your business. Not for you personally, but for your company's finances, your production setup, and your ability to actually deliver what you're selling.

Think of it like this. Any random person can walk into a hospital and say, "I'm a doctor." Nobody believes them without a medical degree and a license to back it up. Vendor Assessment works the same way for sellers on GeM. It's the government's way of confirming you're a real, capable, financially sound business before letting you bid on certain high-stakes orders.

It's mandatory mainly for OEMs (Original Equipment Manufacturers) who want to list products in what GeM calls Q1 and Q2 categories. These are usually higher-value or higher-risk product categories where the buyer needs extra confidence that the seller won't disappear halfway through an order.
If you've been reading up on this topic, you've probably seen the name QCI (Quality Council of India) mentioned everywhere. That's not wrong, exactly. It's just outdated.

For years, QCI handled Vendor Assessment on GeM. Then, in 2024, GeM shifted this responsibility to RITES Ltd: Rail India Technical and Economic Service, a government-owned engineering consultancy with decades of technical inspection experience. Today, RITES is the one reviewing your documents, running your video assessment, and issuing your VA certificate.

Why does this matter to you? Because a lot of blogs, forums, and even some consultants still talk about "QCI Vendor Assessment" like it's current. Old fee structures, old contact details, and old process steps float around online, and following them wastes your time. If you're applying today, RITES is who you're dealing with.
Not every seller on GeM needs to go through this. Here's who does:
OEMs listing products in Q1 or Q2 categories
Sellers managing resellers through the OEM panel
Businesses that want the "VA Verified" tag on their profile, which genuinely builds buyer trust

If you're a trader, a reseller, or a service provider outside these categories, Vendor Assessment is usually optional for you, but it isn’t a blocker. That said, even where it isn't mandatory, many sellers choose to complete it anyway, simply because buyers trust a VA-verified profile more.

One thing worth knowing: your seller category changes how this applies to you. If you're not sure whether you're registering as an OEM or a reseller, it's worth reading our breakdown of OEM vs Authorised Reseller on GeM before you go further, because the two paths diverge quite a bit from here.
